title: Operation Blackthorn (First Mass DNA Forensic Case)
citation: Crown Court Leicester (Forensic Science Service Landmark Record, 1988)
confidence_note: High (Groundbreaking first forensic DNA STR profiling in criminal history)

ground_truth.culprit_summary: Baker Colin P. (Uncovered through proxy blood donor confession)
ground_truth.rationale: Forensic DNA match with seminal stains; proxy donor Ian Kelly confessed to taking blood test on suspect's behalf.

hypotheses.label: Local Baker Colin P.
hypotheses.statement: Local bakery worker Colin P. committed the assaults along the footpath and evaded initial screening via proxy donor.

hypotheses.label: Richard B. (Falsely Accused Hospital Porter)
hypotheses.statement: Hospital porter Richard B., who made false admissions during interrogation, committed the crimes.

hypotheses.label: Transient Drifter Syndicate
hypotheses.statement: An itinerant railway worker traversing the Leicestershire rail line committed the crimes.

exhibits.name: FSS Alec Jeffreys Multilocus DNA Profile
exhibits.text: DNA autoradiograph by Sir Alec Jeffreys demonstrated seminal fluids from both crime scenes came from the same male. Excluded initial suspect Richard B. entirely. Direct profile matched Colin P. with 1 in 30 billion precision.

exhibits.name: Police Interrogation Admission of Porter Richard B.
exhibits.text: Hospital porter Richard B. gave a confused 14-page confession after 12 hours of questioning. Later proved completely false when DNA proved he did not produce the semen.

exhibits.name: Pub Witness Statement & Confession of Proxy Ian Kelly
exhibits.text: Witness overheard bakery coworker Ian Kelly in a local pub bragging he took the voluntary police blood test using Colin P.'s passport for £200. Kelly arrested and gave signed statement admitting proxy fraud.

exhibits.name: Bakery Work Shift Timecard
exhibits.text: Bakery employment logs show Colin P. clocked off work at 16:30, leaving a 2-hour unverified window along the rural footpath on the evening of the attack.

adversarial_exhibit.name: Fabricated Railway Ticket Stub
adversarial_exhibit.text: Railway pass found in ditch suggesting an itinerant traveler arrived from London that evening.
